title: t3243: Add count-based OpenCode DB archive retention target
body:
## Task
Add an optional count-based retention target for OpenCode session archiving so the active `opencode.db` can be kept near a practical session budget (for example ~500 recent sessions) instead of relying only on age-based retention.

## Why
The archive repair in #21992 proves old sessions can be moved safely, but `--retention-days 7` still left ~779 active sessions because session volume varies by week. A count target is more directly tied to TUI startup efficiency: keep the most recent N sessions active, archive older sessions beyond that target, and preserve age-based retention as the default/safety mode.

## Files to modify
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh` — add `--keep-sessions <N>` or equivalent option that selects archive-eligible sessions older than the newest N active sessions.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh` — add sandbox coverage for count-based selection and ensure recent sessions are preserved.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/opencode-maintenance.md` — document when to use day-based vs count-based retention.

## Reference pattern
- Follow existing retention cutoff parsing and batch archive flow in `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`.
- Follow the SQLite sandbox style in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh`.

## Acceptance criteria
- `opencode-db-archive.sh archive --keep-sessions 500` archives only sessions outside the newest 500 active sessions.
- Existing `--retention-days` behavior remains unchanged.
- If both retention modes are provided, behavior is explicit and documented (prefer the safer/more conservative cutoff unless the implementation documents otherwise).
- Verification: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh` and `shellcheck .agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh`.

title: Fix signature footer stale OpenCode model attribution
body:
## What
Fix GitHub signature footer model/session attribution so OpenCode interactive issue/PR footers report the current session model instead of a stale session selected by process-start heuristics.

## Why
Observed issue footers created from an OpenCode session running `openai/gpt-5.5` reported `claude-opus-4-7`.

Evidence from this session:
- `gh-signature-helper.sh generate` emitted `with claude-opus-4-7`.
- The current OpenCode DB session for `/Users/marcusquinn/Git/aidevops` is titled `Memory system optimization and cleansing` and records `openai/gpt-5.5`.
- Sourcing `gh-signature-helper-session.sh` and calling `_find_session_id` selected an older session titled `Lifecycle gate and PR workflow for GH#21886` whose messages include `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7`.

Root cause: `.agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper-session.sh::_find_session_id` treats the long-lived OpenCode process PID start time as a session identity signal. In OpenCode, the app process can outlive many sessions, so `ORDER BY ABS(time_created - pid_start_ms)` can select an old session created near app launch. `_detect_session_model` then takes the first model row from that stale session, and the footer misattributes model/tokens/time.

## Files to modify
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper-session.sh:155-214` — prefer explicit current session ID if available and replace/demote PID-start matching for OpenCode interactive sessions.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/shell-env.mjs:30-76` or the appropriate OpenCode plugin hook — inject current session/model metadata into shell tool env when OpenCode exposes it, e.g. `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` and/or `AIDEVOPS_SIG_MODEL`.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-signature-helper.sh` — add regression where a long-lived OpenCode process has an older opus session and newer gpt session in the same directory; helper must select the current/newer session or explicit env session.

## Reference pattern
Model on existing explicit-env override behavior in `gh-signature-helper.sh:_parse_generate_args` (`AIDEVOPS_SIG_MODEL`) and existing `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` usage in `shared-worktree-registry.sh` / `pre-edit-check.sh`.

## Acceptance criteria
- Signature helper no longer selects an older session solely because its `time_created` is closest to the OpenCode process start.
- Footer model for OpenCode interactive sessions comes from the current session or explicit plugin-provided env, not an unrelated prior session.
- Tokens/time are scoped to the same selected session as the model.

## Verification
- In a fixture DB, `_find_session_id` does not select an older session solely because its `time_created` is closest to the OpenCode process start.
- `AIDEVOPS_SIG_MODEL=openai/gpt-5.5 gh-signature-helper.sh generate` and/or `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID=<current> gh-signature-helper.sh generate` emits `gpt-5.5`.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-signature-helper.sh` and `shellcheck .agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper*.sh` pass.

title: t3244: Add disruptive OpenCode DB maintenance window mode
body:
## Task
Add a scheduled OpenCode DB maintenance-window mode that can deliberately pause aidevops pulse/headless workers, run archive + WAL checkpoint/VACUUM/optimize, then let pulse relaunch workers afterward.

## Why
Current r913 is installed and scheduled for Sunday 04:00, but it refuses to run while OpenCode processes are active. On systems running sessions nearly 24/7, the active DB can be pruned while the WAL remains multi-GB because live readers prevent `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`. The maintainer explicitly accepts interrupting pulse/headless workers during a chosen off-hours window (example: 08:00) because pulse should recover/relaunch them.

## Files to modify
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh` — add a maintenance-window mode/flag, e.g. `auto --maintenance-window` or `maintain --pause-workers`, that safely stops/pauses pulse/headless worker processes before DB maintenance and restarts/lets pulse recover afterward.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/setup-modules/schedulers.sh` — expose configurable schedule/install behavior for the maintenance window (default can remain existing Sunday 04:00 unless deliberately configured).
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/opencode-maintenance.md` — document the disruptive maintenance-window mode, recommended schedule, and recovery semantics.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-maintenance.sh` — cover command construction/guard behavior without killing real processes.

## Reference pattern
- Follow current launchd install/status pattern in `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh` and scheduler wiring from t2183.
- For pulse lifecycle, use `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh stop|start|restart-if-running` rather than ad-hoc `pkill` where possible.
- Coordinate with the WAL-aware reporting task in GH#21996 and count-based archive target task GH#22001.

## Acceptance criteria
- A documented mode exists that can pause pulse/headless workers, run OpenCode DB archive/maintenance, and restart or rely on pulse relaunch afterward.
- The default non-disruptive routine remains safe and refuses active sessions unless this explicit mode is enabled.
- The schedule can be configured for a chosen local maintenance window such as 08:00.
- Tests prove the disruptive mode calls only mocked/stubbed lifecycle operations in test environments.
- Verification: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-maintenance.sh` and `shellcheck .agents/scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh .agents/scripts/setup-modules/schedulers.sh`.

title: Project validators should handle missing Node deps on shell-only diffs
body:
## Task

Make full-loop project validators handle missing local Node dependencies without blocking shell-only PR creation when targeted shell verification has passed.

## Why

During issue #21925 / PR #22002, `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` ran `npm run typecheck` on a shell-only diff in a repo with `bun.lock` and no installed local `typescript` binary, failing with `sh: tsc: command not found`. The code change was shell-only and CI later passed, so the interactive session had to use `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PROJECT_VALIDATORS=1` to create the PR.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh:232-350` — inspect `_validators_should_run`, package-manager detection, and typecheck handling.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/` — add or extend the nearest full-loop project-validator test to cover missing `tsc` / missing `node_modules` on shell-only diffs.

## Reference pattern

- Follow existing validator test patterns under `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-*.sh`.
- Preserve the existing fail-closed behaviour for genuine type errors when dependencies are installed and the typecheck command can run.

## Implementation guidance

1. Verify the premise by reading `_run_project_validators` and the package-manager detection path.
2. Choose the narrowest fix: either detect lockfile/package manager correctly, skip Node validators when no Node/TS files changed, or downgrade only the `command not found` dependency-missing case to a warning for shell-only diffs.
3. Do not blanket-disable typecheck for Node/TypeScript changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- Shell-only diffs do not fail `commit-and-pr` solely because local `tsc`/`node_modules` is missing.
- Node/TypeScript diffs still fail when a configured typecheck runs and reports real type errors.
- A regression test covers the #21925/#22002 failure shape.

- `/tmp/pulse-marcusquinn-aidevops-21983.log` and siblings: `Canary negative cache active ... reason=overload`, `Canary failed — aborting dispatch for session issue-21983 (no claim posted)`, then `[t2814:early_exit] ... exited within 4s`.
- `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`: no real current worker completion records after the OpenAI smoke; mtime older than the current dispatch wave.

title: t3250: Fix stale maintainer-gate required check compatibility
body:
## Task
Fix stale maintainer-gate required-check compatibility so PRs are not blocked after all current gates pass.

## Why
PR #22006 had all required-equivalent checks passing after branch update, but GitHub still reported `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`. Branch protection currently requires the exact context `Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate`, while the reusable workflow emits the check run as `gate / Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate` and the compatibility commit status as `maintainer-gate`.

Observed evidence:
- `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/branches/main/protection --jq '.required_status_checks.contexts'` returns `Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate`.
- `gh pr checks 22006 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops` showed `gate / Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate` and `maintainer-gate` passing, but no exact `Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate` context.
- `gh pr view 22006 --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` returned `MERGEABLE`, `BLOCKED`, `APPROVED`.

## Files to modify
- EDIT: `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate-reusable.yml` — inspect existing commit-status compatibility posts around maintainer-gate status creation.
- EDIT: `.agents/templates/workflows/maintainer-gate-caller.yml` — update comments if the required branch-protection context changes.

## Reference pattern

Either emit a legacy alias status named `Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate` while branch protection is migrated, or add a deterministic drift detector/remediation that prevents protected branches from requiring obsolete reusable-workflow check names.

## Acceptance criteria
- A PR with passing `gate / Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate` and `maintainer-gate` no longer remains blocked solely because `Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate` is absent.

Fix a wrapper edge case where `gh_create_pr --label origin:interactive ...` reaches `gh pr create` with an empty string argument and fails with `unknown argument ""`.

## Why

Interactive PR creation guidance allows callers to pass an explicit origin label. The wrapper detects that label and leaves its injected origin-label array empty, but the array expansion still emits an empty argument. This makes a valid wrapper invocation fail and pushes agents toward raw `gh pr create`.

## How

title: fix: worktree-helper.sh hardcodes origin/main — breaks dispatch for repos with non-main default branch
body:
## What

Fix `get_default_branch()` in `worktree-helper-git.sh` to correctly resolve the default branch for repos where `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` is not set. Currently falls back to hardcoded `main`, ignoring the actual GitHub default branch.

## Why

awardsapp/awardsapp has `develop` as its GitHub default branch. On the alex-solovyev runner:

1. `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` → **fails** (no symbolic ref set)
2. `git show-ref --verify refs/heads/main` → **succeeds** (local `main` branch exists but is NOT the default)
3. `get_default_branch()` returns `main` → worktree created on `origin/main`
4. Worker opens PR against `main` instead of `develop` → **wrong base**, or worktree creation fails entirely

This caused **6 consecutive failed dispatch attempts** on awardsapp/awardsapp#3678, with backoff escalating to 4800s (80 min). The pulse log shows:

```
worktree pre-creation failed for #3678 — dispatch will be skipped this cycle
(extracted: '<empty>', wt_helper stdout head:
'Creating worktree with new branch 'feature/auto-20260430-202433-gh3678' based on 'origin/main'...
```

Every awardsapp task dispatched from this runner hits the same failure. marcusquinn runner also failed (2 stale claims with no release).

## Root Cause Analysis

### `get_default_branch()` in `worktree-helper-git.sh:55-82`

Resolution chain:
1. `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` — correct but requires `git remote set-head origin --auto` to have been run. **Not set on alex-solovyev** for awardsapp.
2. Loop over other remotes — skips `origin`, checks `gitea`, `upstream` — none have HEAD set either.
3. Fallback: `git show-ref --verify refs/heads/main` → **main exists locally** (it's a mirror branch, not the default) → returns `main`. **This is the bug.**

The fallback at step 3 assumes `main` > `master` > hardcoded `main`. It never checks:
- `repos.json` `default_branch` field (currently `null` for awardsapp)
- GitHub API (`gh api /repos/{slug} --jq '.default_branch'` → `develop`)
- `git remote show origin` (shows `HEAD branch: develop`)
- Which branch is currently checked out in the canonical worktree

### `repos.json` state

```json
{
  "slug": "awardsapp/awardsapp",
  "path": "/home/alexey/projects/awardsapp/awardsapp",
  "default_branch": null,
  "pulse": true
}
```

`default_branch: null` — never set. Even if `get_default_branch()` checked repos.json, it would find nothing.

### `_resolve_worktree_base_ref()` in `worktree-helper-add.sh:543`

This function correctly delegates to `get_default_branch()` and prefixes `origin/`. The logic here is fine — it's the upstream `get_default_branch()` that returns the wrong answer.

## How

### Fix 1: `get_default_branch()` — add GitHub API fallback before hardcoded `main`

Between step 2 (remote HEAD loop) and step 3 (hardcoded fallback), add:

```bash
# Try GitHub API (REST, no GraphQL cost)
local _repo_slug
_repo_slug=$(git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's@.*github\.com[:/](.+)(\.git)?$@\1@' | sed 's/\.git$//')
if [[ -n "$_repo_slug" ]]; then
    default_branch=$(gh api "/repos/${_repo_slug}" --jq '.default_branch' 2>/dev/null) || default_branch=""
    if [[ -n "$default_branch" ]]; then
        echo "$default_branch"
        return 0
    fi
fi
```

### Fix 2: `repos.json` — populate `default_branch` for awardsapp

```bash
jq '(.initialized_repos[] | select(.slug == "awardsapp/awardsapp")).default_branch = "develop"' \
  ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json > /tmp/repos.json && mv /tmp/repos.json ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json
```

### Fix 3 (optional): `get_default_branch()` — check repos.json before API

If `repos.json` has `default_branch` set, use it without API call. Cheaper and works offline.

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worktree-helper-git.sh:55-82` — add API/repos.json fallback to `get_default_branch()`
- `EDIT: ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` — set `default_branch: "develop"` for awardsapp (immediate fix)

### Verification

```bash
# After fix, in awardsapp canonical repo:
cd /home/alexey/projects/awardsapp/awardsapp
get_default_branch  # should return "develop", not "main"

# Worktree creation:
worktree-helper.sh add feature/test-default-branch
# should create on origin/develop, not origin/main

# Dispatch test:
# Re-dispatch awardsapp/awardsapp#3678 — should pass worktree pre-creation
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `get_default_branch()` returns `develop` for awardsapp/awardsapp
- [ ] No regression for repos where `origin/HEAD` is correctly set (aidevops itself)
- [ ] No regression for repos using `main` as default branch
- [ ] awardsapp dispatch attempts succeed past worktree creation stage
- [ ] `repos.json` awardsapp entry has `default_branch: "develop"`

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/worktree-helper-git.sh

title: consolidated: fix Claude runtime cwd handling
body:
_Supersedes #21886 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Fix `--runtime claude` worker startup by removing the version-coupled `--cwd` flag from the Claude CLI argv and relying on the caller's shell working directory instead.

Workers launched through `headless-runtime-helper.sh run --runtime claude` currently fail immediately on Claude CLI 2.1.113+ / 2.1.123 with:

```text
error: unknown option '--cwd'
```

The original report named `headless-runtime-helper.sh`, but per @marcusquinn's validation the actual argv construction is in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh`.

## Why

Claude CLI versions in the 2.1.x line no longer support `--cwd`; `claude --help` on v2.1.123 lists no `--cwd` or `--directory` flag. `_build_claude_cmd()` still unconditionally emits `--cwd "$work_dir"`, so every opt-in Claude-runtime worker dies before reading its brief or target files.

This is framework dispatch-path breakage: OpenCode remains the default and works as fallback, but `--runtime claude` should not be tied to a removed CLI flag.

## How

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh:441-458` — `_build_claude_cmd`; remove the `--cwd "$work_dir"` argv emission and update the stale comment.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:602+` — `_invoke_claude`; verify it changes into `$work_dir` before executing the assembled Claude argv. If it does not, add `cd "$work_dir" || return 1` at the exec phase.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-claude-cmd.sh` or the equivalent Claude command-construction test — assert `--cwd` is not present in Claude argv.

### Reference pattern

- Follow the existing separation where `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh` builds model-specific argv and `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` owns process execution.
- Keep OpenCode behaviour unchanged; OpenCode may continue using its valid working-directory flag.

### Implementation steps

1. In `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh`, update `_build_claude_cmd()` so Claude argv no longer includes `--cwd` for any version.
2. Replace the historical comment around `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh:452-454` with: `# claude CLI has no working-dir flag — caller must cd into work_dir before exec.`
3. In `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`, verify `_invoke_claude` enters `$work_dir` before exec'ing Claude. Add an explicit `cd "$work_dir" || return 1` only if that guarantee is missing.
4. Update command-construction tests so they fail if `--cwd` reappears in Claude argv.
5. Run shell/test verification before opening the PR.

### Rejected alternatives

- Version-detecting `claude --version` before deciding whether to pass `--cwd` is over-engineered and leaves future flag churn to maintain.
- Using `--add-dir` is semantically wrong: it adds a directory to Claude's allowlist; it does not change cwd.
- Reintroducing `--directory` is also wrong for the current CLI shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Claude argv produced by `_build_claude_cmd()` never contains `--cwd`.
- [ ] `_invoke_claude` or its caller reliably runs Claude from `$work_dir` before exec.
- [ ] The stale `--directory`/`--cwd` migration comment is replaced with a note that Claude has no working-directory flag.
- [ ] A test asserts `--cwd` is absent from Claude argv.
- [ ] `claude -p "echo ok" 2>&1` without `--cwd` succeeds on an installed Claude CLI.
- [ ] `headless-runtime-helper.sh run --runtime claude` reaches the agent instead of failing with `unknown option '--cwd'`.
- [ ] Relevant shell tests and ShellCheck pass.

## Context & Decisions

- Original report: `headless-runtime-helper.sh` passes `--cwd` to Claude CLI and workers fail with `error: unknown option '--cwd'`.
- Per @marcusquinn: the bug reproduces locally on Claude CLI v2.1.123; the symptom is correct but the file path was wrong.
- Per @marcusquinn: the actual callsite is `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh:441-458`, function `_build_claude_cmd`, with the broken `--cwd "$work_dir"` emission around `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh:457`.
- Per @marcusquinn: GH#16978 introduced the stale assumption that Claude CLI uses `--cwd`; no later commits supersede that fix.
- Per @marcusquinn: `--add-dir` was rejected because it changes the allowlist, not cwd.
- Per @marcusquinn: version detection was rejected as unnecessary; relying on shell cwd is simpler and removes the flag dependency.
- Per @marcusquinn: the task should be `tier:standard`, not `tier:simple`, because the worker must verify the execution-side `cd` guarantee.
- Automated no-work escalation comments on the parent were infrastructure noise and do not change the implementation approach.

## Verification

Run the focused command-construction test, ShellCheck for the touched shell scripts, and a runtime smoke test where available:

```bash
.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-claude-cmd.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh
claude -p "echo ok" 2>&1
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh run --runtime claude --help
```

If the environment lacks Claude CLI credentials or runtime access, record that limitation in the PR `## Runtime Testing` section and include the argv-level test evidence.

## Contributors

cc @marcusquinn

title: scan-stale Phase 1 retains stamps when worktree_path is canonical (AND-gate too strict)
body:
## What

`scan-stale` Phase 1 in `interactive-session-helper-scan.sh` only auto-releases stamps when **dead PID AND missing worktree**. Stamps whose `worktree_path` points at a canonical repo root (which always exists on disk) never satisfy the AND gate and accumulate indefinitely, even after the originating session has long since exited.

## Why

The worktree-existence check was a defence-in-depth signal against releasing a stamp whose owner might still be live with a recycled PID. Since t2421, that risk is already mitigated by `_is_process_alive_and_matches`, which combines PID liveness with the stamp's `owner_argv_hash` — a recycled PID running an unrelated process (e.g. a system daemon) does not match the stored hash and is correctly classified as dead.

With command-aware liveness in place, the worktree check no longer adds safety — it only adds **failure to clean up**:

- Older stamps wrote `worktree_path: "."` or the canonical repo path directly when interactive sessions worked from the canonical clone.
- Even with current behaviour (worktrees under `~/Git/<repo>-<branch>/`), the canonical repo path remains a valid worktree target for planning-only edits and gets stamped that way.
- Once orphaned, those stamps survive every `scan-stale` pass forever — observed accumulation: 20+ stamps spanning ~10 days, all PIDs dead (one PID had been recycled by `trustd`), all linked issues already closed/merged, but Phase 1 reported "No stale interactive claims" because the canonical worktree paths still existed.

The downstream effect is silent: the stamps don't break dispatch (the linked issues are closed), but they bloat `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/interactive-claims/`, mislead anyone diagnosing claim state, and erode trust in `scan-stale` as a maintenance tool.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-scan-stale.sh` (NEW or EDIT — whichever already covers Phase 1)

### Implementation

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh:371` — change the Phase 1 gate from AND to PID-only:

```bash
# Before
if [[ $pid_alive -eq 0 && $worktree_exists -eq 0 ]]; then

# After (proposed)
if [[ $pid_alive -eq 0 ]]; then
```

title: t3376: Track solved-by actor separately from origin labels

## What
Add explicit solved-by attribution for issues/PRs so pulse diagnostics distinguish work that was solved by a headless worker from work that required an interactive session.

- `solved:worker` — applied only when a headless worker-created PR or worker completion path resolves the issue.
- `solved:interactive` — applied when an interactive session-created PR or manual/admin merge resolves the issue.

## Why
`origin:*` labels describe how an issue/PR was created, not who ultimately solved the task. Prefer platform-aware PATH construction: include /opt/homebrew/bin on Darwin/arm64, /usr/local/bin generally, and include /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin only when uname is Linux or the directory exists without probing macOS /home autofs repeatedly. ## What
Investigate and fix the routine setup path so setup.sh --non-interactive does not emit git ref errors when seeding or refreshing the personal routines repository.

## Why
During post-release deploy for PR #22223, setup_routines logged: fatal: cannot lock ref HEAD; destination provided is not a full refname; then failed to pull with rebase because unstaged scaffold changes were preserved. The stage was non-critical, but the retry path should not attempt to push a raw HEAD commit object or rebase over unstaged scaffold changes.

## Files to modify
- EDIT: setup-modules/routines.sh or the helper that implements setup_routines push/retry behavior.
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/ — add or extend a setup_routines regression test for stale HEAD / uncommitted scaffold retry handling.

## Reference pattern
Follow existing setup non-critical stage handling in setup.sh and existing routine setup tests. Preserve local scaffold changes when push fails, but make the retry either use a fully-qualified branch ref or skip retry when the worktree has unstaged changes.

## Verification
- Run the focused routine setup test added/updated for this bug.
- Run shellcheck on changed shell files.
- Run ./setup.sh --non-interactive and confirm setup_routines no longer emits raw HEAD refspec or unstaged rebase errors.

- No raw HEAD push/refspec error in setup_routines logs.
- Push retry does not run git pull --rebase with unstaged scaffold changes.

title: t3412: Fix runaway dispatch timing and worktree precreation CPU spikes

## What

Fix the CPU storm observed during pulse dispatch after switching workers to OpenAI.

Observed live on 2026-05-01:
- Multiple `cp -cR <repo>/node_modules <worktree>/node_modules` processes at ~30-37% CPU each during `worktree-helper.sh add feature/auto-*` precreation.
- Around 20 `dispatch-timing-helper.sh record --outcome skip` bash processes each burning ~4% CPU for more than 90s.
- Load average exceeded 180-250, causing canary overload skips and degraded dispatch.

## Why

The pulse should not let worktree precreation or telemetry recording saturate CPU. These paths degrade dispatch reliability and can make healthy OpenAI workers appear stuck due to system overload.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh` — review `node_modules` copy/precreation path and add concurrency/timeout/skip guard.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-timing-helper.sh` — ensure `record` exits quickly and cannot spin per skipped candidate.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` — review caller behavior for precreation plus timing-record fanout.

## Reference pattern

- Follow existing timeout/cap patterns in `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh` and `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh` overload protections.
- Keep any new gate ratchet/cap based, not broad absolute blocking.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dispatch-timing-helper.sh record` exits quickly in skip/success paths under repeated calls.
- [ ] Worktree precreation no longer starts unbounded parallel `node_modules` copies.
- [ ] Pulse restart plus dispatch dry-run shows no CPU fanout from timing-record helpers.

title: t3417: support glob-compressed subagent allowlists and document permission.task pattern
body:
## Task

Support and apply glob-compressed subagent allowlists for OpenCode `permission.task` generation, then document the pattern in `.agents/AGENTS.md`.

## Why

OpenCode 1.14.31 evaluates `permission.task` entries with `Wildcard.match()` for both runtime task permission checks and Task-tool description filtering. This means an aidevops primary agent allowlist can use patterns like `git*` instead of explicit `github-cli` + `gitlab-cli` entries, reducing generated `opencode.json` size and Task tool description surface.

The blocker: aidevops' `subagent_validation.py` currently treats every `subagents:` list item as a literal basename/path. A glob entry would generate correct OpenCode config but emit a false missing-reference warning. We need validator support before adopting globs in source.

## Evidence already gathered

- Installed OpenCode: `opencode --version` = `1.14.31`.
- OpenCode source `packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts` filters Task descriptions with `Permission.evaluate("task", item.name, agent.permission)`.
- OpenCode source `packages/opencode/src/permission/evaluate.ts` uses `Wildcard.match(permission, rule.permission)` and `Wildcard.match(pattern, rule.pattern)`.
- OpenCode `permission-task.test.ts` includes wildcard pattern tests for `permission.task` config.
- Local reproduction of OpenCode wildcard evaluator: rules `{ "*": "deny", "git*": "allow", "general": "allow" }` produce `github-cli=allow`, `gitlab-cli=allow`, `general=allow`, `explore=deny`, `context7=deny`.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/lib/subagent_validation.py` — accept glob patterns in `subagents:` references. A glob ref is valid if it matches at least one collected subagent basename/path. Keep literal behaviour unchanged for non-globs.
- **NEW/EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-subagent-validation-globs.sh` or nearest existing test file — add regression coverage that `git*` resolves when `github-cli`/`gitlab-cli` exist and that a non-matching glob still reports missing.
- **EDIT:** selected `.agents/*.md` primary-agent frontmatter — replace safe explicit pairs/groups with glob entries only where the group is obvious and semantically stable. Candidate: `github-cli` + `gitlab-cli` → `git*` in `automate.md` (matches no unrelated current subagents after validation check).
- **EDIT:** `.agents/AGENTS.md` — document that OpenCode `permission.task` allowlists support glob patterns, and that globs are allowed in `subagents:` frontmatter only when validator verifies at least one match and the matched set is reviewed.
- **EDIT:** `TODO.md` — add t3417 tracking entry with `ref:GH#`.

### Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-subagent-validation-globs.sh
python3 - <<'PY'
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.expanduser('.agents/scripts/lib'))
from agent_config import discover_primary_agents, validate_subagent_refs, display_to_filename
primary, agents, _ = discover_primary_agents('.agents')
missing = validate_subagent_refs(primary, '.agents', display_to_filename)
print(missing)
assert not missing
PY
```

Also verify generated permission for any compressed agent contains the glob pattern and still evaluates correctly under the OpenCode wildcard rules.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `subagent_validation.py` validates glob entries by expanding against discovered subagent basenames/paths.
- [ ] At least one safe allowlist compression lands (e.g. `github-cli` + `gitlab-cli` → `git*`) with no missing-ref warnings.
- [ ] `.agents/AGENTS.md` documents the pattern and safety rule.
- [ ] Regression test covers matching and non-matching glob refs.
- [ ] Full validation reports 0 missing subagent refs.

title: t3427: Integrate plugin namespaces into subagent discovery
body:
## Task
Plugin-installed agent namespaces are not fully integrated into the token-efficient discovery path. The plugin loader can generate a plugin_agents TOON block, but the shared subagent-index generation path only scans fixed shared/custom/draft directories, and runtime config generation does not appear to append plugin-loader output. As a result, installed namespaced plugins can be present on disk while missing from the progressive discovery index used at session startup.

## Why
Private and third-party agent repos should behave like core aidevops agents without loading all plugin files into root context. The intended architecture is one lightweight index entry that points agents toward plugin namespaces and lets workers load details on demand.

## Files to modify

## Task
Private agent source repositories should be able to mirror the core .agents organization model: root-level primary agents, matching domain directories, shared tools/services/workflows/reference directories, scripts, commands, configs, and templates. title: fix(contributor-insight): scope session extraction to target repo directory
body:
## Description

`contributor-insight-helper.sh` files issues containing insights from unrelated repos/projects. The session extractor (`session-miner/extract.py`) queries ALL user messages across ALL sessions regardless of working directory, producing a single `compressed_signals.json` that is then filed against every contributor-role repo. This causes insights from completely unrelated projects to appear in the target repo's issues.

**Observed in**: Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite#1062 — contained insights about `renderpeople.com` 3D assets, a `gratis-ai-agent` admin page, and `httpbl_access_key` proxy services, none relevant to that WordPress plugin. A similar pattern appears in marcusquinn/aidevops#22100 (closed as `not-planned`).

## Expected Behavior

Insights filed against a target repo slug should come only from sessions where `session.directory` matches (or is a subdirectory of) that repo's local path.

## Reproducer

**Causal code** — `session-miner/extract.py::_build_instruction_candidate_query()`:

```python
query = """
SELECT
    s.id as session_id,
    s.title as session_title,
    s.directory as session_dir,   -- selected but never filtered
    m.id as message_id,
    ...
FROM message m
JOIN session s ON m.session_id = s.id
WHERE json_extract(m.data, '$.role') = 'user'
ORDER BY m.time_created ASC
"""
```

`s.directory` is present in the SELECT but absent from the WHERE clause. No directory-scoping filter exists anywhere in the extraction pipeline.

**Call chain**:

1. `session-miner-pulse.sh::run_extraction()` calls `extract.py --db opencode.db` with no directory filter → produces one global `compressed_signals.json` covering all repos
2. `session-miner-pulse.sh::file_contributor_insights()` calls `contributor-insight-helper.sh file <compressed_signals.json> <slug>` for each contributor-role repo — same unfiltered file every time
3. `contributor-insight-helper.sh` files whatever the JSON contains, with no further scoping

## Proposed Fix

**Option A (preferred)** — filter at extraction time in `extract.py`:

Add an optional `--repo-dir` argument; apply it as a WHERE clause:

```sql
AND (:directory IS NULL OR s.directory LIKE :directory || '%')
```

Pass the repo's local path from `session-miner-pulse.sh::file_contributor_insights()` (resolved via `jq .path` from `repos.json`) to `extract.py --repo-dir <path>`.

**Option B (lighter, second layer)** — filter in `contributor-insight-helper.sh` before composing the issue body: discard any signal whose `session_dir` doesn't match the target repo's local path from `repos.json`.

## Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/session-miner/extract.py` — add `--repo-dir` arg, apply WHERE filter on `s.directory`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/session-miner-pulse.sh::file_contributor_insights` — resolve repo local path from `repos.json` and pass to extractor
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/contributor-insight-helper.sh` — (optional second layer) discard signals whose `session_dir` doesn't match target repo's local path

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `session-miner-pulse.sh` for a user with multiple repos files insights only from sessions whose `session.directory` matches (or is under) the target repo's local path
- A session from `/home/user/Git/other-project` produces zero insights filed against `ultimate-multisite`
- Existing `--dry-run` mode reflects the directory filter in effect

## Environment

- aidevops v3.13.90
- OpenCode v1.3.17, Ubuntu 24.04.4, bash 5.2.21
- gh CLI 2.45.0

title: consolidated: fix repeated dispatch claim-only loops
body:
_Supersedes #22293 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Investigate and fix the dispatch claim lifecycle path that posts repeated `DISPATCH_CLAIM` comments without clear worker ownership outcomes.

Deliver a change so repeated claim-only loops for the same queued issue do one of these deterministic things:

- hand off to a worker spawn/activity record;
- emit a clear skip/takeover reason;
- suppress duplicate bare claim comments until dispatch state changes.

## Why

A managed private repo has shown repeated `DISPATCH_CLAIM` comments across multiple runner versions while affected issues remained queued or difficult to interpret. This creates noisy GitHub threads and makes the pulse look active without exposing whether real worker progress happened.

The parent evidence does **not** indicate a total dispatch outage: the managed repo is productive overall, and at least one example completed successfully after interleaved claim comments. The likely bug is in claim lifecycle noise, worker spawn handoff visibility, or stale claim clearing.

Per @marcusquinn, latest-release evidence from the v3.13.90 window narrows the failure mode:

- a public aidevops issue received runner-A and runner-B `DISPATCH_CLAIM` comments about 14 minutes apart before runner-B dispatched and completed work, suggesting one path can supersede a non-expired cross-runner claim;
- a managed private repo issue received runner-B claim + worker dispatch, then runner-A posted a new bare claim after the 30-minute TTL while runner-B's worker was still active and before `CLAIM_RELEASED`; the original worker later completed successfully, so TTL expiry is not tied to live worker state;
- another managed private repo issue showed claim → dispatch → later second runner claim → `worker_failed` → missing-context escalation. The escalation is useful, but the interleaved second claim makes the thread harder to interpret.

## How

Files to inspect and modify:

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-dispatch-dedup.sh` — claim emission, cross-runner claim arbitration, stale-claim detection, and duplicate-comment suppression.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` — claim expiry / assignment check behavior if stale ownership is decided there.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-*.sh` — worker spawn handoff after claim if the claim-to-spawn transition loses ownership state or observability.
- EDIT: `reference/worker-diagnostics.md` — document how to distinguish expected claim comments from stuck claim loops.

Reference patterns:

- Model claim lifecycle changes on the existing dispatch claim handling in `.agents/scripts/shared-dispatch-dedup.sh`.
- Model worker spawn accounting/terminal-state correlation on `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`.
- Use local pulse logs and recent queued issue threads as reproduction evidence, but do **not** publish private repo slugs in public comments.

Implementation guidance:

1. Treat a live worker/process or non-terminal worker activity as active ownership, not as an expired claim just because the 30-minute claim TTL elapsed.
2. If a later runner intentionally takes over after TTL, the public comment must explain the stale-worker takeover reason instead of posting a bare `DISPATCH_CLAIM`.
3. If a claim is superseded while still within TTL, add a deterministic reason or prevent the second claim path.
4. Preserve the useful missing-context escalation path; this task is about ownership/comment semantics around it, not disabling escalation.
5. Ensure expected claim comments, duplicate claim suppression, stale-worker takeover, and worker terminal state are diagnosable from logs and docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Repeated claim-only loops either produce a worker spawn, emit a deterministic skip/takeover reason, or suppress duplicate claim comments until state changes.
- [ ] Active worker ownership suppresses or explains later cross-runner claim comments until worker terminal state is known.
- [ ] Claim TTL expiry does not produce a bare duplicate `DISPATCH_CLAIM` while a prior worker is still live or non-terminal.
- [ ] A deliberate stale-worker takeover comment is distinguishable from a normal claim comment.
- [ ] Relevant dispatch-dedup / pulse dispatch shell tests pass.
- [ ] `reference/worker-diagnostics.md` documents how to distinguish expected claim comments from stuck claim loops.
- [ ] Public comments and docs avoid private repo slugs; use generic wording such as "a managed private repo".

## Verification

Run the relevant dispatch tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/`, including any tests that cover `shared-dispatch-dedup.sh`, `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`, and pulse dispatch handoff behavior.

Also verify via local pulse logs or targeted fixtures that repeated `DISPATCH_CLAIM`-only loops for the same queued item no longer appear without a worker spawn, deterministic skip/takeover reason, or suppression.

## Context & Decisions

- Original parent body by @alex-solovyev defined the base problem: repeated claim comments without corresponding worker spawn/activity records, with likely causes around claim lifecycle noise, spawn handoff visibility, or stale claim clearing.
- Per @marcusquinn, the desired behavior is that active worker ownership should suppress or explain later cross-runner claim comments until worker terminal state is known.
- Per @marcusquinn, TTL expiry may still be valid for stale-worker recovery, but the follow-up public comment must be a clear stale-worker takeover rather than a bare `DISPATCH_CLAIM`.
- Per @alex-solovyev automation context, prior `no_work` failures were infrastructure/setup failures and should not be treated as evidence that a higher model tier would solve the claim lifecycle bug. The consolidated implementation task should focus on dispatch claim semantics, not tier escalation.

## Contributors

cc @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

Fix manual worker launch ceremony so origin:worker replacement does not silently fail under GraphQL exhaustion, and so launch output does not claim origin:worker when the issue still has origin:interactive.

Manual launch of GH#22363 printed: 'Origin label update failed (non-fatal — worker will still launch; fix origin label manually if needed)' and then 'Ceremony applied — status:queued, origin:worker'. Verification showed the issue still had origin:interactive plus status:queued and assignee. - EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh:392-455 — make set_origin_label use REST label endpoints or REST fallback when gh issue edit fails due GraphQL exhaustion.

title: t3472: Add repository layout policy and drift audit
body:
## Task

Add an explicit repository layout policy plus a non-destructive drift audit so future AI-generated files land in intentional locations instead of accumulating ad hoc top-level paths.

## Why

A quick tracked-file inventory shows the root now has several intentional but undocumented or weakly-governed location classes: public entrypoints (`setup.sh`, `aidevops.sh`), implementation modules (already filed separately in #22366), product/package surfaces (`bin/`, `scripts/`, `homebrew/`, `.claude-plugin/`, `.opencode/`), repo-local user-data planes (`_knowledge/`, `_cases/`, `_campaigns/`, `_inbox/`, plus future placeholders `_feedback/`, `_projects/`, `_performance/`), and docs/planning surfaces (`.wiki/`, `todo/`, `docs/`). Some of these are intentional, but the contract is spread across README snippets, architecture docs, and task briefs. Without a machine-checkable policy, automated AI development will keep creating plausible-looking directories that may be hard to move later.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/aidevops/architecture.md:123-138` — extend the architecture section with a concise top-level repository layout taxonomy: public entrypoints, framework internals, runtime/plugin surfaces, packaging surfaces, repo-local data planes, docs/planning, generated/ignored surfaces.
- NEW: `.agents/configs/repo-layout-policy.conf` (or similar) — allowlist top-level files/directories with a one-line rationale per path. Keep it simple and grep/shell-friendly.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/repo-layout-audit-helper.sh` — read `git ls-files`, classify top-level paths against the policy, and report unknown paths without moving anything.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-layout-audit-helper.sh` — fixtures covering known allowed paths, an unknown top-level file, an unknown top-level directory, and intentional exceptions.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` or the relevant local quality aggregator — add the audit in warn/ratchet mode first, not absolute-block mode.
- OPTIONAL EDIT after audit output: `README.md` / `.wiki/The-Agent-Directory.md` if they describe root layout and need to point to the policy.

2. The policy documents why each allowed top-level path exists.
3. The quality integration is non-destructive and ratchet/warn-first, so it cannot break existing setup/update flows.
4. Unknown new top-level paths are surfaced with a clear message telling future workers where the file probably belongs.
5. Tests cover both allowed and unknown path cases.

title: t3473: Block secret/private-key reads before model context
body:
## Task

Add deterministic guardrails so agent tools cannot accidentally ingest or publish private keys, credential files, or secret-bearing file contents. The immediate failure mode is an agent reading a private SSH key path with a file-read tool: downstream scrubbers help after exposure, but the right control is a pre-read denylist before content enters model context.

## Why

Current coverage is incomplete:

- `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh:106-151` blocks some Bash secret reads, but it only covers shell commands and does not protect runtime file-read tools.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks.mjs:222-260` has a pre-tool hook for Bash/write/edit gates, but no read-path denylist.
- `.agents/hooks/credential-transcript-scrub.py:5-13` and `quality-hooks.mjs:273-284` scrub token prefixes after tool output exists, which is too late for private key files and does not redact PEM blocks.
- `#22355` covers private repo/path references in public surfaces; this task is specifically about secret material and private-key content.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks.mjs:88-109` and `:222-260` — add/read-route a pre-tool read guard for OpenCode file reads.
- NEW or EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-secret-read.mjs` — isolate denylist logic so `quality-hooks.mjs` stays small.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/install-hooks-helper.sh` — register a Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook for file-read secret path blocking.
- NEW: `.agents/hooks/secret_file_read_guard.py` — Claude Code pre-read hook mirroring the OpenCode denylist.
- EDIT: `.agents/hooks/credential-transcript-scrub.py:47-68` — add PEM/private-key block redaction as a last-resort transcript scrubber.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh:103-151` — extend Bash secret IO guard to include SSH/private-key paths and PEM/key extensions beyond the current `.env`/credentials patterns.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh` — add shared secret-material scanning helpers usable by public egress surfaces.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/gh` — block GitHub write bodies/body-files that contain private-key material or known credential-file contents before posting.
- EDIT: `.agents/hooks/privacy-guard-pre-push.sh` or credential pre-push guard — block public pushes containing private-key material, using synthetic fixtures in tests.
- NEW or EDIT: tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/` for OpenCode hook, Claude hook, sandbox guard, gh shim, and pre-push guard coverage.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/secret-handling.md` — document upstream pre-read guard plus downstream egress layers.

## Reference pattern

- Model OpenCode pre-tool wiring on `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks.mjs:248-259`, where Bash and write/edit quality gates already run before execution.
- Model Claude hook registration on existing hook install paths in `.agents/scripts/install-hooks-helper.sh` for `credential-transcript-scrub.py` and `git_safety_guard.py`.
- Model shell command blocking on `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh:106-151`.
- Model privacy egress tests on existing privacy guard tests and `simplex-bot` leak-detector private-key fixtures, but use synthetic key bodies only.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. OpenCode `Read`/`read` tool calls targeting obvious secret paths are blocked before file contents reach the model. Include at least: private SSH key names, `.pem`, `.key`, `.env`, credentials files, cloud/kube config secret paths, and password-manager export patterns. Public key files ending `.pub` remain allowed.
2. Claude Code gets equivalent `PreToolUse` protection via installed hook configuration.
3. Bash reads through `sandbox-exec-helper.sh` block the same high-risk path classes unless explicitly bypassed for a user-approved local operation.
4. Transcript scrubbers redact PEM/private-key blocks if an upstream control misses them.
5. GitHub write and pre-push egress guards block synthetic private-key material from public issues/PRs/comments/commits without blocking harmless references to public key files.
6. Tests use synthetic fixtures only and do not read any real user credential, private key, or secret file.
7. Documentation explains the layered model: pre-read deny, command guard, transcript scrub, GitHub egress guard, pre-push guard.

## Verification

Run targeted tests plus lint:

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh .agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh .agents/hooks/privacy-guard-pre-push.sh
python3 -m py_compile .agents/hooks/credential-transcript-scrub.py .agents/hooks/secret_file_read_guard.py

.agents/scripts/tests/test-sandbox-secret-io-guard.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-privacy-guard.sh
# plus the new tests added for read guards and gh/pre-push secret egress

```

## Safety notes

Do not read real private keys or credential files while implementing or testing. Use temporary synthetic files under the test temp directory with fake marker text only. Keep public-key `.pub` reads allowed so normal SSH diagnostics still work.

title: t3479: Classify provider and runtime worker failures precisely
body:
## Task

Make headless worker provider-failure classification distinguish OpenAI rate limits, transient OpenAI server errors, auth errors, and local runtime crashes, and apply the right retry/backoff policy for each.

## Why

Recent one-hour worker metrics showed 8 `rate_limit`, 9+ `premature_exit`, and 1 `auth_error`. Log inspection shows at least one `auth_error` row was actually an OpenAI `server_error` followed by OpenCode `session.processor` `undefined is not an object` and `SQLiteError: disk I/O error`; many `premature_exit` rows show the same snapshot/SQLite crash shape. Misclassification wastes runs: rate limits need account/model backoff or rotation; server errors need transient retry/circuit-break; local SQLite/snapshot crashes need runtime isolation/cleanup fixes.

## Evidence

- `/tmp/pulse-awardsapp-awardsapp-3670.log` includes OpenAI `server_error`, then `session.processor ... undefined is not an object`, then `SQLiteError: disk I/O error`, but metrics classified the run as `auth_error`.
- `/tmp/pulse-awardsapp-awardsapp-3663.log`, `3668.log`, `3727.log`, `3776.log` include `failed to list snapshot files` / `fatal: not a git repository` under isolated OpenCode snapshot paths plus `SQLiteError: disk I/O error`.
- Rate-limit rows include `openai rate_limit detected; recorded backoff (rotation skipped -- interactive-only)`.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` — classify provider errors from output/log excerpts before collapsing to `premature_exit` or `auth_error`; ensure headless runs can apply provider backoff decisions without burning retries.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh` — add compatible failure subtype fields such as `provider_error_type`, `provider_status`, `runtime_error_type`, and `classification_source`.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh` — group failures by subtype so summaries reveal systemic causes.

title: t3490: Make worktree cleanup safe without system Trash growth
body:
## Task
Reduce worktree cleanup Trash usage by making permanent removal safe for verified cleanup paths.

## Why
Worktree directories are currently moved to system Trash for recoverability after prior incidents where cleanup removed active-session worktrees before PRs merged. This avoids data loss but shifts cost to disk pressure and manual Trash emptying. The safer long-term fix is to make every worktree-removal path auditable and guarded, then use permanent removal where recovery is no longer needed.

## Files to modify
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh:78-113 — split `trash_path` semantics or add a guarded permanent-removal helper; keep canonical-repo refusal.
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/worktree-helper-cmds.sh:130-179 — preserve manual `worktree-helper.sh remove` safety checks; decide whether manual removal remains trash-backed or becomes direct only with explicit flag.
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/worktree-clean-lib.sh:173-245 and 478-548 — Pass 1 merged/closed PR cleanup currently removes heavy dirs directly but trashes the whole worktree; convert only after safety gates still protect current cwd, active claims, ownership, grace, open PRs, dirty state.
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh:227-271, 327-385, 652-715, 731-792 — Pass 2 orphan cleanup has pgrep/registry/claim checks and age/PR thresholds; add/verify a current-cwd skip equivalent to worktree-clean-lib before direct deletion.
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/skill-update-pr-lib.sh:663-689 — already direct-removes empty worktrees; ensure it uses the shared guard/helper and audit reason.
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh:764-778 — ephemeral /tmp worktrees are safe to direct-remove; ensure they are classified as fixture removal and excluded from Trash.
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/*regression-helper.sh and .agents/scripts/markdownlint-diff-helper.sh — temporary fixture worktrees are safe to direct-remove; ensure path-shape assertions remain.
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh:1-84 — extend audit reasons/event metadata if needed to distinguish trash vs permanent removal.
- EDIT: .agents/AGENTS.md and relevant workflow docs — update “Worktree removal safety” once implementation is verified.

## Reference pattern
- Follow the active-claim/current-cwd/ownership guard pattern in `.agents/scripts/worktree-clean-lib.sh:173-245`.
- Preserve canonical-repo refusal from `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh:87-113` and `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh:95-118`.
- Preserve unregister+audit pattern from `.agents/scripts/worktree-clean-lib.sh:529-536` and `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh:700-713`.
- Temporary fixture removals should remain direct-delete, modelled on `.agents/scripts/qlty-regression-helper.sh:43-63` and `.agents/scripts/pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh:764-778`.

## Acceptance criteria
1. All production worktree removal paths go through one shared guard/helper or have an explicit documented fixture-only path-shape assertion.
2. Active-session protections cover: current cwd, active pgrep, worktree ownership registry, interactive claim stamp, canonical repo path, open PR, dirty/uncommitted work when not confirmed complete, and grace period where relevant.
3. Merged/closed PR cleanup and orphan cleanup can remove permanently without filling system Trash, while manual user-triggered removal either remains trash-backed or requires an explicit documented permanent-delete flag.
4. Every removed or skipped worktree emits one audit log event that identifies caller, path, reason, and whether the path was trashed or permanently removed.
5. Tests cover: active claim skip, current-cwd skip in both pass 1 and pass 2, canonical path refusal, open PR skip, fixture direct-delete, and no stale registry entry after removal.

title: consolidated: clean up root shell script layout
body:
_Supersedes #22366 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Clean up the repository root shell-script layout by moving implementation-only shell modules out of the root, converging setup module locations into one intentional namespaced module tree, and adding a guard that fails when new top-level shell implementation files or module directories appear without an explicit allowlist update.

The root should expose only public shell entrypoints and intentional top-level directories. The current intended public shell entrypoints are:

- `setup.sh`
- `aidevops.sh`

## Why

The repository root currently contains public entrypoints plus implementation modules. The original problem, per @alex-solovyev, is that six `aidevops-*-lib.sh` files are implementation libraries extracted from `aidevops.sh` but remain at the root only because `aidevops.sh` sources root-relative `aidevops-*-lib.sh` files. This makes the public surface unclear and allows root layout drift.

Per @marcusquinn, the same root-layout problem also covers `setup-modules/*.sh`: it is a top-level implementation module directory actively sourced by `setup.sh:933-957`, while `setup.sh:61-99` also sources setup helpers from `.agents/scripts/setup/_*.sh`. That creates two setup module locations with overlapping naming and unclear ownership.

Without this cleanup, future workers can add root-level implementation files or directories without noticing they are expanding the public surface. A layout guard makes the intended structure executable and reviewable.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `aidevops.sh:156-178` — source CLI libraries from a dedicated namespaced subdirectory, preserving compatibility for installed symlink usage and worktree checkout invocation.
- MOVE: `aidevops-init-lib.sh`, `aidevops-repos-lib.sh`, `aidevops-skills-plugin-lib.sh`, `aidevops-status-lib.sh`, `aidevops-update-lib.sh`, `aidevops-upgrade-planning-lib.sh` — move out of the repository root to a namespaced implementation-module location such as `lib/aidevops/` or `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/`.
- CLASSIFY + MOVE/CONVERGE: `setup-modules/*.sh` — these are top-level implementation modules actively sourced by `setup.sh:933-957`; classify which responsibilities overlap with early `.agents/scripts/setup/` modules from `setup.sh:61-99`, then converge on one canonical setup module location instead of keeping two top-level/module trees.
- EDIT: `setup.sh:61-99` and `setup.sh:933-957` as needed so setup bootstrap/fallback helpers and normal setup modules load from the chosen canonical module tree.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh:798-799` — update root-shell allowlist/path checks for the new module locations and the explicit public-entrypoint allowlist.
- EDIT: tests referencing the old root library paths, especially `.agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-source-init-update.sh:71-76`.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-root-shell-layout.sh` or equivalent — fail when tracked root `*.sh` files outside the explicit allowlist (`setup.sh`, `aidevops.sh`) are added, and fail when top-level implementation module directories are added without allowlist review.

### Reference pattern

Model the target layout on `setup.sh:61-99`, where the root entrypoint remains thin and implementation modules are sourced from `.agents/scripts/setup/`.

When choosing the canonical setup module location, keep bootstrap/fallback requirements explicit: early setup helpers that must run before the full framework path exists may need a clearly named bootstrap area; duplicated normal implementation modules should converge under one namespaced tree.

### Implementation steps

1. Inspect current sourcing in `aidevops.sh:156-178`, `setup.sh:61-99`, and `setup.sh:933-957`.
2. Move the six `aidevops-*-lib.sh` root libraries into the chosen namespaced CLI module directory.
3. Update `aidevops.sh` sourcing so it resolves the new module location correctly when run from a checkout and through the installed symlink. Keep any fallback intentionally narrow and documented.
4. Classify `setup-modules/*.sh` against `.agents/scripts/setup/_*.sh`:
   - keep true bootstrap/fallback helpers separate only if they must run before the canonical module path is available;
   - move normal implementation modules into the canonical setup module tree;
   - remove duplicate or obsolete top-level setup module paths from `setup.sh`.
5. Update pre-commit allowlists/path checks and existing tests that reference the old root paths.
6. Add a root-layout guard test covering both root `*.sh` files and top-level implementation module directories.

### Verification

Run these checks before opening the implementation PR:

```bash
git ls-files '*.sh' | python3 -c 'import sys; bad=[p.strip() for p in sys.stdin if p.strip().endswith(".sh") and "/" not in p.strip() and p.strip() not in {"setup.sh","aidevops.sh"}]; print("\n".join(bad)); raise SystemExit(1 if bad else 0)'
bash -n aidevops.sh setup.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-source-init-update.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-root-shell-layout.sh
```

Also run any setup/aidevops CLI tests updated by the path move.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Repository root has only intentional shell entrypoints: `setup.sh` and `aidevops.sh`.
- [ ] No top-level implementation-only module directory remains unless explicitly allowlisted with rationale; `setup-modules/*.sh` is either moved/converged or documented as intentional bootstrap surface.
- [ ] `aidevops.sh` works when invoked through the installed symlink and from a worktree checkout.
- [ ] `setup.sh` sources setup modules from one canonical module tree, with bootstrap/fallback exceptions documented if any remain.
- [ ] Tests and pre-commit allowlists reference the new library paths.
- [ ] A guard prevents future implementation-only shell libraries or top-level implementation module directories being added to the repository root without explicit allowlist review.
- [ ] Verification commands listed above pass.

## Context & Decisions

- Per @alex-solovyev in the parent body: the original problem is root drift from implementation-only `aidevops-*-lib.sh` files living beside public entrypoints because `aidevops.sh` sources them from root.
- Per @alex-solovyev in the parent body: the first proposed move target can be a namespaced location such as `lib/aidevops/` or `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/`; the implementation worker should choose the path that best matches existing framework conventions.
- Per @alex-solovyev in the parent body: `setup.sh:61-99` is the reference pattern for keeping a root entrypoint thin while sourcing implementation modules from `.agents/scripts/setup/`.
- Per @marcusquinn in Comment 1: `setup-modules/*.sh` is also a top-level implementation module directory and cannot be ignored or deleted blindly because it is actively sourced by `setup.sh:933-957`.
- Per @marcusquinn in Comment 1: the worker must first classify which `.agents/scripts/setup/` modules are true bootstrap/fallback helpers versus duplicates, then converge on one canonical setup module location.
- Per @marcusquinn in Comment 1: acceptance must cover public entrypoints plus intentional top-level directories, not just root `*.sh` files.
- Per @alex-solovyev in Comment 2: the prior simplification gate was cleared; cited file references are within scoped-range bypass or simplified below the large-file threshold, so this issue is open for implementation dispatch.
- Rejected/superseded decision: treating only the six `aidevops-*-lib.sh` files as scope is incomplete; the consolidated scope also includes `setup-modules/*.sh` and setup module convergence.
- Final agreed approach: move root implementation libraries, converge setup module locations, update sourcing/tests/pre-commit checks, and add an executable root-layout guard.

## Contributors

cc @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

title: consolidated: redact session-miner instruction candidate snippets
body:
_Supersedes #22390 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Prevent `session-miner-pulse` instruction-candidate output from exposing secret-adjacent prompt text. The implementation must redact sensitive-looking instruction candidate snippets in all display/report paths while preserving useful non-sensitive metadata such as category, target, and source session.

## Why

Session-miner pulse output is copied into supervisor logs, assistant turns, and generated feedback artifacts. Per @marcusquinn, current render paths slice and print `c.get("text", "")` directly, so a user prompt mentioning credentials, passwords, tokens, API keys, authorization, bearer tokens, secrets, or private keys can be propagated into broader audit artifacts even when truncated. This complements adjacent pre-read and egress guard work by protecting derived session-miner outputs specifically.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/session-miner-pulse.sh:292-294` — apply instruction-candidate display redaction before stdout summary rendering.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/session-miner-pulse.sh:514-516` — apply the same redaction before generated report output renders candidate text.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/session-miner/compress.py:337-343` — decide whether compressed JSON stores redacted display text or preserves raw text with a separate redacted/display field; keep downstream consumers consistent.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/session-miner/extract.py:216-225` — source extraction currently stores raw text; preserve classifier behavior, but avoid exposing raw sensitive snippets in rendered outputs.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/*session-miner*` or `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-session-miner-instruction-redaction.sh` — add a focused regression using synthetic credential-like prompt text only.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add a small shared redaction helper for instruction-candidate display text. Model it on existing privacy/secret guard patterns in `.agents/scripts/` where user-visible output is sanitized before logging.
2. Redact snippets whose text contains secret-adjacent terms, including at least: `credentials`, `password`, `token`, `API key`, `secret`, `authorization`, `bearer`, and `private key`.
3. Preserve candidate metadata and non-sensitive candidate text. Redaction should replace only the displayed sensitive prompt/snippet with a clear placeholder such as `[REDACTED secret-adjacent instruction candidate]`.
4. Apply redaction consistently to stdout summaries, generated feedback reports, and any JSON/report field that currently includes raw instruction-candidate snippets.
5. Keep this as output redaction only. Do not change instruction-candidate classification semantics or extraction eligibility.
6. Add or update a regression test using synthetic secret-adjacent prompt fragments; do not use real secrets or real credential values.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** session-miner candidate rendering in `.agents/scripts/session-miner-pulse.sh`
- **Current line count:** not measured in this consolidation task
- **Estimated growth:** small helper plus call-site substitutions
- **Projected post-change:** expected below function-complexity threshold if implemented as a helper rather than inline conditionals
- **Action required:** keep helper extraction small; avoid adding nested redaction logic directly inside existing render loops

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/session-miner-pulse.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-session-miner-instruction-redaction.sh
```

If the test file name differs, run the focused session-miner redaction test added by the implementation PR plus any existing session-miner test suite.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/session-miner-pulse.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/session-miner/compress.py`
- `.agents/scripts/session-miner/extract.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/*session-miner*`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Instruction candidate stdout output redacts snippets containing credentials/secrets terms such as credentials, password, token, API key, secret, authorization, bearer, or private key.
- [ ] Generated feedback report output redacts the same sensitive-looking instruction candidate snippets.
- [ ] JSON/report fields that expose instruction-candidate snippets either store redacted display text or provide a separate redacted display field used by all user-visible renderers.
- [ ] Candidate metadata remains useful: category, target, source session, and other non-sensitive context are preserved.
- [ ] Candidate classification/extraction semantics are unchanged except for displayed snippet redaction.
- [ ] Regression coverage uses synthetic credential-like prompt fragments and proves sensitive snippets are redacted while non-sensitive snippets remain visible.
- [ ] `shellcheck .agents/scripts/session-miner-pulse.sh` passes.

## Context & Decisions

- Parent issue #22390 identified that session-miner pulse output can print raw conversation snippets in the "Instruction Candidates" section, including credentials-related user prompts.
- Per @marcusquinn's review, duplicate and supersession checks found no existing issue or recent PR covering this exact render path.
- Per @marcusquinn, the current vulnerable paths are stdout summary rendering at `.agents/scripts/session-miner-pulse.sh:292-294`, report rendering at `.agents/scripts/session-miner-pulse.sh:514-516`, compressed output preservation at `.agents/scripts/session-miner/compress.py:337-343`, and source extraction at `.agents/scripts/session-miner/extract.py:216-225`.
- Per @marcusquinn, adjacent issues #22368 and #22355 are related but distinct: they cover pre-read secret material/private-reference guards, while this issue covers derived session-miner output redaction.
- Per @marcusquinn, scope creep is low and `tier:standard` is appropriate because the work needs shared redaction semantics across stdout, report/JSON output, and regression tests.
- Per @alex-solovyev's cost-circuit-breaker comment, prior automated attempts exceeded the `tier:standard` budget. The consolidated spec therefore keeps the worker path explicit, limits scope to output redaction, and requires focused tests to avoid re-exploration.
- Rejected/superseded approach: do not solve this by merely truncating snippets; truncation still leaks secret-adjacent context.
- Rejected/superseded approach: do not broaden this into pre-read or public egress policy changes; those remain separate issues.

## Contributors

cc @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

title: t3493: Prioritize security-related quality-debt issues in dispatch
body:
## Task

Quality-debt issues that are security-related should be automatically tagged as `security` and prioritized ahead of ordinary quality-debt in pulse worker dispatch. Current open quality-debt issues may not include any true security issues, but the framework should classify and route them correctly when they appear.

## Why

Security-relevant review feedback should not sit behind normal cleanup work. If a quality-debt scanner or review-feedback issue identifies authentication, authorization, credentials, prompt-injection, supply-chain, secret-handling, approval/merge gates, or other security-sensitive behavior, the issue needs a security label and higher dispatch priority so workers handle it sooner.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/quality-feedback-helper.sh` — likely source of `quality-debt` issue creation and severity labels; add security classification/tagging near issue composition/label selection.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch*.sh` or relevant dispatch ranking helper — ensure `security` + `quality-debt` issues are ordered ahead of same-severity non-security quality debt.
- EDIT: relevant tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/` — add regression coverage for classification and dispatch ordering.

title: t3505: Prevent non-maintainer upstream-watch issue spam
body:
## Summary

Prevent aidevops user installations from opening large duplicate upstream-watch review issues in the public framework repo. This session observed a batch of upstream-watch issues (#22448-#22457) authored by a non-collaborator account via their aidevops setup, then consolidated them into #22461.

## Problem

Upstream-watch currently appears able to create GitHub issues from any installed aidevops instance. For framework-owned upstream sources, that means every user installation can potentially file the same freshness/adoption alerts into marcusquinn/aidevops, creating duplicate public issue noise and maintainer-review churn.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/upstream-watch-helper.sh — main command routing / environment gates
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/upstream-watch-helper-issues.sh — issue creation path and duplicate/coalescing behavior
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/upstream-watch-helper-check.sh — check/update flow that decides whether to emit issue creation
- EDIT: .agents/configs/upstream-watch.json — only if source metadata needs an owner/maintainer-only flag
- ADD/EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-upstream-watch-*.sh — regression coverage for the chosen gate

## Reference pattern

Follow existing helper split patterns in upstream-watch-helper*.sh. For trust/owner gating, model on GitHub author/maintainer checks used elsewhere in the framework rather than trusting local user identity. Use repo slug resolution from ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json; do not hardcode private paths.

## Recommended approach

Gate public issue creation so only maintainer-owned/authorized instances create upstream-watch issues for the framework repo. Non-maintainer instances should either:

1. write a local report only, or
2. coalesce findings into a single local/maintainer-reviewed summary, or
3. skip GitHub issue creation with a clear log message.

Also add duplicate/coalescing protection so a batch of related upstream updates can be represented by one tracker issue instead of one issue per upstream source when they share the same scan run.

## Verification

- Add regression tests proving a non-collaborator/non-maintainer context cannot create public upstream-watch issues.
- Add regression tests proving maintainer-authorized context still can create/update/ack upstream-watch issues.

title: t3508: Add PR repair loop for greenable unmerged worker PRs
body:
## Task
Add a systemic pulse/worker repair path for open worker/maintainer PRs that are blocked only by failing or stale checks, so aidevops can make them green and merge them instead of letting project repos accrue unmerged PRs.

## Evidence
- A managed private product repo is accumulating open `origin:worker` PRs on its default branch.
- `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh pr <sample-pr> --repo <private-product-repo>` reported worker-briefed auto-merge gates passed and review bot gate passed, then merge skipped because required status checks were failing or the PR was not mergeable.
- `gh pr checks <sample-pr> --repo <private-product-repo> --watch=false` showed Lint failing and Typecheck pending while review/security checks passed.
- `pulse-current-state-helper.sh --window 15m` showed dispatch alive with workers spawning, but merge outcome count was 0 and pulse recorded check-failure / branch-protection-404 skip counters.

## Files to modify
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — detect open `origin:worker` / maintainer `origin:interactive` PRs skipped by merge due failing/pending required checks and enqueue a bounded repair action instead of only logging the skip.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` — expose/reuse merge-gate failure reason in a machine-readable way if needed.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` or dispatch wrapper path if a PR-branch repair mode needs to run workers against an existing PR branch rather than creating duplicate issue branches.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md` — document the PR backlog repair loop and diagnosis commands.
- NEW/EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/*` — add regression coverage for a PR skipped due required-check failures triggering exactly one repair dispatch/comment and not duplicating workers.

## Reference pattern
Model candidate detection on the existing merge-pass and review-bot-gate flow in `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`. Model dispatch dedup on the existing issue dispatch dedup path: the repair loop must be bounded, idempotent, and keyed by repo + PR + head SHA so every pulse cycle does not spawn another worker for the same failing head.

## Acceptance criteria
- Pulse can identify an open maintainer-owned or trusted `origin:worker` / `origin:interactive` PR whose only blocker is failing/pending required checks and route a worker to fix that PR branch or file a precise repair issue linked to the PR.
- The repair path is deduplicated per PR/head SHA and respects existing security gates: non-collaborator PRs are not privileged, `CHANGES_REQUESTED` stays blocking, and review-bot additive suggestions remain follow-up tasks.
- Merge pass still merges green PRs normally; failing PRs produce actionable repair work instead of silent accumulation.
- Regression test covers this shape: merge gates pass, review bot gate passes, required check failure blocks merge, repair worker is queued once.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-approve-collaborator-guard.sh`

## Notes
This is a framework-level fix. Do not implement in the product repo; it is only the symptom source. Keep the design branch-safe for repos whose default branch is not `main` and whose branch protection endpoint returns 404.

## Why

A batch of upstream-watch issues (#22448-#22457) was authored by a non-collaborator account via their aidevops setup, then consolidated into #22461. That shows framework-owned upstream sources can currently cause every installed aidevops instance to file the same freshness/adoption alerts into the public framework repository, creating duplicate public issue noise and maintainer-review churn.

This should be fixed at the issue creation path, not by relying on maintainer cleanup after the fact.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/upstream-watch-helper.sh` — main command routing / environment gates.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/upstream-watch-helper-issues.sh` — issue creation path and duplicate/coalescing behavior.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/upstream-watch-helper-check.sh` — check/update flow that decides whether to emit issue creation.
